correctness.rationale: In the degree-zero localization at z_i z_j, the listed single-vertex replacement ratios generate: each other edge either replaces both endpoints within their original parts (u_p v_q), or brings in one vertex of the omitted part (u_p s_r or v_q t_r). The exponents at nonbase vertices of the first two parts recover each free-generator exponent. For the remaining variables the Laurent exponent vector encodes the omitted-column totals and the two row counts; successive swaps between columns connect all monomials with those margins, giving exactly the 2x2 minors. Thus the isomorphism is a chart isomorphism, not only an identity of tangent cones. A nonzero matrix entry permits elimination and gives smoothness of the rank-one locus; the vertex has tangent dimension 2w versus dimension w+1 for w>=2, and w=1 is smooth. The zero cone factor is precisely the Segre coordinate chart on the relevant supported edge type. The three supports are disjoint in projective space, and the charts cover X. This gives the dimension, the codimension w+1, the stated projective Segre degree, and the example's dimensions and multiplicities. Normality and CM are standard for these determinantal charts. The degree-d basis is indexed by d+1 row counts and binomial(d+w-1,w-1) column margins, giving leading Hilbert multiplicity w. For the local class and canonical obstruction, one can use the small resolution of the rank-one cone by the total space of O(-1)^w on P^1. Its Picard group is generated by O(1); it agrees with the affine Weil class group since the non-isomorphism loci have codimension >=2. The class still has infinite order after localizing at a point of the singular stratum, as its pullback restricts to degree one on the exceptional fiber P^1 over that point's residue field. Localization is surjective on class groups. The canonical bundle on this resolution has class w-2, giving the torsion-free Q-Cartier test; the argument is unchanged on multiplying by affine space. In the only singular Gorenstein case w=2 the cone is a hypersurface node: blowing up its vertex gives a smooth resolution with exceptional P^1 x P^1 and discrepancy 1 by adjunction and normal bundle O(-1,-1), proving terminality, also after the smooth product. The supplied script and notes describe bounded representative chart, Hilbert count and Jacobian checks; they were read, not executed, and are not needed for the universal proof.

originality.rationale: A distinct earlier indexed complete-multipartite theorem explicitly gives the same entire affine charts, the disjoint embedded singular Segres, and transverse codimension, multiplicity, class group and Q-Gorenstein test. Setting the number of parts to three is a direct specialization. The earlier statement uses C; the same monomial and minor presentation works over the integers and the same geometric checks over any algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, so the field extension is not a substantive new phenomenon. The global cutoff and terminality are routine consequences of those charts and the known threefold node, not a surviving independent contribution. The failure is due to demonstrated coverage, not access to the 2000 paper.
residual_risks: The 2000 full text may provide further prior coverage. Bibliographic priority was not independently established beyond the actual compared records. These limits do not weaken the direct earlier indexed formula match.
